newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice prices stable in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice prices stable in light trade.

text.p: Vietnamese rice prices have remained stable this week in light trade as buyers continue to look elsewhere for supplies, dealers said on Thursday.
Five percent broken grade rice was quoted at around $270-$273 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, unchanged from a week earlier as buyers continue to look for supplies from Pakistan and other origins.
Ten percent broken grade was quoted at 10 dollars per tonne below this level.
Dealers said they were expecting news to emerge soon of a possible deal between the Philippines and Vietnam, involving the purchase of as much as 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of local rice.
They said a Philippine official had visited Vietnam last week and traders were anticipating an announcement ahead of the Tet Lunar New Year holiday, which begins on February 6.
Currently only one vessel is in Saigon port, with a shipment bound for Iraq.
Traders said the only significant recent deal had been the sale last week of 90,000 tonnes for March or April shipment to Indonesia.
